evidence: Plin. NH 10.132: Phāsiānae avēs (Lewis & Short s.v. Phāsis)
terms.comment: The bird of the river Phasis in Colchis: Martial’s Phāsides volucrēs (13.45.1, Lewis & Short).
The masculine, which Lewis & Short calls the more frequent form.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 52, 140, 144.
